title: Avatar: Seven Havens Isn’t Seen as a “Kids Show,” Producers Explain
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens might be approachable for younger audiences and fans of all ages, but those behind the series don’t really see it as just a show for kids. Avatar: The Last Airbender originally kicked off the franchise with Nickelodeon decades ago, and with it introduced animation fans to a whole new kind of world through its run. Then it was taken in an even darker direction with releases like The Legend of Korra and Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender in the years since . For Avatar: Seven Havens , it kind of sits in the middle.

Avatar: Seven Havens might star a very young set of twin Avatars for this new era of the franchise, and it might be designed in a different way than The Legend of Korra , but it takes on some intense subject matter that’s especially seen withe final episodes of the debut season. As executive producer Sehaj Sethi explained in a Reddit AMA for the series, the team always intended to make it “accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers.”

Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Talks the Show’s Darker Themes

“Personally, I think this show really isn’t a kids show,” Sethi stated when asked about whether or not Avatar: Seven Havens was intended for audiences around Pavi and Nisha’s age of 10-11. “The themes we cover are quite dark and mature. We always intended for this show to technically be accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers .” Elaborating on this further, Sethi explained that they’re not holding back on putting Pavi and Nisha through the wringer, “Even though Nisha and Pavi are children, we don’t hold back on making them face truly traumatic experiences.”

Series producer Ethan Spaulding teased that Avatar: Seven Havens is going to get darker from here on out as well, “[T]he show definitely gets darker as the story progresses,” but played coy as to whether or not it has a chance of getting as dark as The Legend of Korra did. Either way, this is something that has already been put in place with the final episodes of the first season as it has tackled xenophobia, isolationism, fear as a result of that and more. With Pavi exploring more Havens in the coming season , we’re bound to see more of these intense topics.

What Does This Mean for Avatar: Seven Havens’ Future?

Avatar: Seven Havens has been in development for the past few years before the first season finally premiered, and speaking to ComicBook, stars Aishu Devan (Nisha) and Saheli Khan (Pavi) revealed that they had been working on the show since they were 10-11 years old themselves. Noting that production on the third and fourth season had already begun, all they could tease was that there would be plenty of “character development” for the twins moving forward. So it seems like Pavi and Nisha are going to age alongside all of the events in the series.

It won’t be too much longer before we see what’s next as Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is already scheduled to kick off its run with Paramount+ beginning on May 21st next year. The new season will be 13 episodes long, and then followed by 13 more episodes with Season 3 releasing later in 2027. The series will then come to an end with Season 4 some time after, so how do you feel about Avatar: Seven Havens right now? Is it a kids show? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Singer/Songwriter Hiromi Ōta Dies at 71
content:
There was a funeral service for close family.

Ōta was born on January 20, 1955 in Tokyo and grew up in Kasukabe, Saitama Prefecture. She made her career debut with the song "Amadare" (Raindrops) in 1974.

She was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019. She was hospitalized for treatment in 2024.

Ōta performed the theme song for the Chocobo Racing game in 1999. Ōta also voiced Belle in the Japanese version of The Stingiest Man in Town animated U.S. special.

title: One Piece’s New Movie Could Change the Anime Forever
content:
One Piece has been airing for more than 25 years, and over its long run, it has become a part of many fans’ lives. However, it could change forever with a new One Piece movie releasing next year. What One Piece became known for was being the longest-running shonen anime, releasing new episodes every Sunday since 1999, with a few breaks here and there. However, that long-running legacy came to an end when, in 2025, it was announced that starting in 2026, the anime would embrace a 26-episode-per-year format, releasing in only two seasons. This brought an end to the legacy the anime had built over 26 years.

This year, fans got their first look at how this new anime format affected the series, and it is evident that the change will keep the anime on air for a longer time, as the pacing remains largely the same as it was under the old format. However, this year also brought new announcements from Toei Animation, revealing that the studio is working on two movies. One of them, One Piece Film: God Valley , is scheduled to release next year and will adapt events from the original source material, something the series has never done before. This signals a change that could transform the One Piece anime forever.

One Piece ‘s New Movie Release Strategy Could Be Devastating for International Fans

Up until now, every One Piece movie produced has featured an original story, something fans could easily skip since it was never aligned with the main storyline. This meant that if an anime movie failed to receive a theatrical release in certain regions for various reasons, it wasn’t a problem. One of the main factors with anime movies is that they first release in Japan, while international fans have to wait at least a couple of months, if not longer, to watch them. This wouldn’t normally be a problem, but with the new One Piece movie being canon and adapting a major narrative, it could be devastating for international fans who want to experience the movie as soon as it releases. This will certainly be a problem for major Western countries, as seen with Demon Slayer .

Even though Demon Slayer is a huge franchise, especially in the movie format, its latest movie took two months to receive an international release. Considering the upcoming One Piece movie will be a theatrical exclusive for some time, potentially for at least six months, fans who miss it in theaters for whatever reason could face a long wait before it becomes available on streaming platforms. Unlike anime episodes, which release weekly, this could create a significant delay. This essentially means that it could take even longer for One Piece to actually come to an end, something that some fans who want the franchise to last longer may consider a blessing in disguise.

Another impact One Piece ‘s new movie could have on the anime is that, if it becomes a huge success, which is certainly possible given its potential, newer arcs of the series could also be adapted into movies rather than episodes. This could follow the recent trend of popular franchises receiving theatrical anime releases, such as Haikyuu and Demon Slayer , particularly for their finales. Only time will tell how the final arc of the anime will be presented to fans, but it is clear that the wait for the franchise to end has already been extended. In many ways, the One Piece anime has already changed forever.

The One Piece Anime Has Officially Changed Forever

When it was announced that the anime would be following a 26-episode-per-year format , it became clear that the old One Piece anime had already come to an end, with a new, modern format being introduced to the franchise. With the new canon adaptation in movie form, the modernization of the anime franchise has become even more evident. Moreover, One Piece has already embraced the modern anime format more than most other series, all thanks to Netflix’s ambitious project: a reboot of the anime. Netflix will release seven episodes adapting the first arc of the series, with all episodes dropping simultaneously.

This will serve as an entry point for new fans of the series going forward, offering a modernized way to experience the story without having to watch Toei Animation’s adaptation, which consists of over 1,000 episodes. This could also encourage Toei Animation to change its strategy for the anime adaptation, potentially fully embracing the movie format for future arcs, with faster pacing and theatrical releases on the big screen. All these elements point toward the anime industry changing forever, and One Piece ‘s new movie format could mean longer waits for international fans to watch canon events, unless the franchise plans simultaneous international releases, a possibility that unfortunately seems unlikely.

title: Miss Konosuba? You Need to Watch Crunchyroll’s Funniest Fall Anime
content:
If you’re missing Konosuba: God’s Blessing on this Wonderful World right now, there’s a new anime now streaming with Crunchyroll this Fall that you really should give a chance. Konosuba has become a standout anime franchise because of the parodical take on Isekai stories . Featuring a group of would-be losers who band together to succeed, it’s basically like watching a team of gremlins failing upwards through their misadventures. The anime adaptation for Asa Rokushima’s The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life perfectly taps into that same energy.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life may not be an Isekai anime series like Konosuba , but the two share a core that feels incredibly familiar. Both anime offer a group of individuals who often devolve into bouts of wild emotional states that alter their character designs , both groups are put into dangerous situations that are taken with various levels of seriousness, and both series are just having a lot of fun with how they progress through their story. It just scratches that same itch.

Why You Should Watch The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is set in a traditional fantasy world ( with teases of something else going on under the surface ) and falls in line with the power-fantasy stories seen in other offerings. Rein is an enchanter who can invest skill points into weapons and armor, but is soon kicked out of his party because he’s seen as unnecessary. Only to then take back all of the points he’s given out thus far and make his paltry clothes and weapons (which are sometimes just pebbles) stronger than anything else.

While it starts out with the same kind of hook that’s usually seen with stories where the main character is kicked out of their party (only to be revealed to be secretly strong), it takes a much floatier route to how it gets to certain points. Rein is naive and a bit of a dullard, but takes his adventures seriously now that he’s on his own. And in comparison to Konosuba, he’s a much more capable person than Kazuma. It’s the same for his party that slowly forms with additions like Lily (an S-Rank adventurer who was a shut-in for two years) and Margaret (who originally wants to kill Lily). The levels just keep building on from there.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life isn’t as wacky as Konosuba when it comes to the nature of its stories, and that’s ultimately what makes it even more compelling. Because while Rein, Lily and Margaret are seen having fun in almost a trolling kind of way with their adventures, there is a great deal of risk involved with the episodes seen thus far. There’s no potential of revivals like Kazuma’s, and thus it keeps the group from turning into full Looney Tunes characters like its counterpart.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Just Looks Great

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is a lot like Konosuba in terms of the tone of its comedy and wacky character choices, but it most comes through in the production. While it’s not as outwardly wacky and fluid as its counterpart, this series has a lot of effort in punctuating the wild scenes with a fun variety in the way it chooses to bring certain scenes to life. Action scenes will move with a cool fluidity then will be countered by the stuff faces of its cast to land the joke.

The series is directed by Shu Honma for P.A. Works, the studio behind anime such as Shirobako, Buddy Daddies, Skip and Loafer and more, and all of that expertise and personality is fueling the series. It leads to a perfect blend of cool action scenes with the hilarious comedy, and often results in an experience that’s rarely seen elsewhere. But with so many new series now airing as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule , this one has likely fallen through the cracks of your watching schedule.

Konosuba: God’s Blessing on this Wonderful World is now in the works on Season 4 of the anime , but has yet to reveal a release date or window as of this time. With no clear indication of just how long the wait for its return is going to be, The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is a good way to scratch that itch for now in the meantime. You can find it now streaming on Crunchyroll with both Japanese and English language audio.

Have you checked out The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life this Fall? If so, what do you think of it so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Sumikko Gurashi Franchise's New Switch 2 Game Launches on November 19
content:
A new game in the Sumikko Gurashi franchise titled Sumikkogurashi Welcome to Poka Poka Onsen ( Sumikko Gurashi Pokapoka Onsen ni Yо̄koso ) launches on Thursday for Nintendo Switch 2.

In the game, players run a hot spring with the Sumikko. There are furniture, decorations, outfits, collectibles, and minigames.

Sumikkogurashi Create a Wonderful Sumikko Island! ( Sumikko Gurashi Tsukurou! Sutekina Sumikko Shima ) launched for Nintendo Switch in November 2025. In the game, players work together with the other creatures to develop the island. Players can fulfill quests and grow crops across four seasons.

The second film in San-X 's Sumikko Gurashi franchise , Eiga Sumikko Gurashi: Aoi Tsukiyo no Mahō no Ko (The Magical Child of the Blue Moonlit Night), received a Switch game in December 2021.

The fourth film in the franchise , Eiga Sumikko Gurashi: Sora no Ōkoku to Futari no Ko (The Sky Kingdom and the Two Children), opened in theaters in October 2025.

The franchise is getting a fifth anime film in 2027.

Sumikko Gurashi debuted in 2012 as slightly negative characters who like to stay in the corner of a room. The characters include "Shirokuma," a polar bear who is sensitive to cold; "Penguin?" (with a question mark in its name), a penguin who is unsure if it is actually a penguin; "Tonkatsu," a piece of pork cutlet that was left uneaten; "Neko," a shy cat; and "Tokage," who hides his nature as one of the last dinosaurs.

title: Dragon Ball Super’s Manga Deserves to Return From Hiatus to End Its Story
content:
Dragon Ball Super has been on an indefinite hiatus for the past two years, and the manga deserves to get a proper grand finale with a return for at least one more arc so fans can say goodbye. Dragon Ball Super is in such a strange place right now when it comes to the franchise on a whole. A new remake anime series is airing new episodes this Fall as it adapts the classic TV anime from the very beginning , and a brand new anime is in the works for the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc.

But even as the anime is back in action with these new projects, they also aren’t technically that “new” in the grand scheme of things. Following the passing of legendary creator Akira Toriyama in 2024, each of the “new” projects for the franchise has been working within the past timeline of the Dragon Ball series. All the while, Dragon Ball Super’ s manga has been on hold with no signs of moving the story forward anytime soon. It just needs to return to resolve its final cliffhanger, at least.

Dragon Ball Super’ s Story Needs to Officially End Before the Anime Catches Up

Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol has been announced as a brand new anime adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc from the Toyotaro illustrated manga series. Unlike the other arcs seen in the series, this arc was entirely new and had not been adapted or inspired by what was seen in the anime. This new arc introduced a powerful new villain, new transformations, and more with the tease of an expanded universe from that point on. Which then continued with another arc, Granolah the Survivor.

These arcs were then followed by the manga’s adaptation of the Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero film, and that’s where the manga left off when it went on hiatus back in 2024 . While it had seemed like a suitable ending at the time due to both Toriyama’s passing and the fact that it was also now set at the final story in the Dragon Ball Super timeline, the anime has thrown a wrench into things that only exacerbate one of the lingering cliffhangers that manga fans have yet to see fully resolved. And the anime is going to reach this cliffhanger sooner than not.

The Granolah the Survivor Arc ends with the reveal that Frieza had become the new strongest warrior in the universe after training in a Hyperbolic Time Chamber he stumbled on in space, and this had been the explanation as to why Goku and Vegeta had been seen training together with Broly on Beerus’ planet during Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . With the anime likely eventually adapting this arc after the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc, its also going to hit the wall of that cliffhanger too. It’s just going to be even tougher of a cliffhanger, however, as by that point it will be the final anime story that fans will see.

Dragon Ball Super Just Needs One Last Arc for Fans to Say Goodbye

The only way to avoid this eventual fate is for Dragon Ball Super ‘s manga to return for at least one final arc to resolve the Black Frieza cliffhanger. It would also serve as a perfect way to say goodbye as one last final fight with arguably Dragon Ball ‘s most iconic villain would also be a great way to bookend how far Dragon Ball Super had evolved from its original incarnation. A godly battle against Frieza (and potentially even more ) with Ultra Instinct Goku and Ultra Ego Vegeta at full mastery will also be a big enough fight to feel like it’s fitting of the franchise’s current scale.

Dragon Ball Super basically opened a can of worms when it introduced gods and a multiverse when it first began, and unfortunately will never really be able to tap into the full potential of such an idea even after everything that has happened. Given that the franchise has been under such a tight lock and key since Toriyama’s passing, all fans could probably hope for is at least one final story to help end the series for good. Artist Toyotaro has never been shy about his wanting to return to the series , so it’s time to make good on that promise.

If the manga never does return to settle the Black Frieza story, there’s a potential the anime moves forward with it instead in the coming years. That’s entirely possible given that now the anime team can technically make brand new materials for the series with releases like Dragon Ball Daima seen before , but that was also the final project supervised by Toriyama. It’s been a complicated web of licenses and rights over the last couple of years, but fans just want a sign that the story will get a proper end.

contentBlocks.text: Dragon Ball Super has been on an indefinite hiatus for the past two years, and the manga deserves to get a proper grand finale with a return for at least one more arc so fans can say goodbye. Dragon Ball Super is in such a strange place right now when it comes to the franchise on a whole. A new remake anime series is airing new episodes this Fall as it adapts the classic TV anime from the very beginning , and a brand new anime is in the works for the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc.

But even as the anime is back in action with these new projects, they also aren’t technically that “new” in the grand scheme of things. Following the passing of legendary creator Akira Toriyama in 2024, each of the “new” projects for the franchise has been working within the past timeline of the Dragon Ball series. All the while, Dragon Ball Super’ s manga has been on hold with no signs of moving the story forward anytime soon. It just needs to return to resolve its final cliffhanger, at least.
Dragon Ball Super’ s Story Needs to Officially End Before the Anime Catches Up

Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol has been announced as a brand new anime adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc from the Toyotaro illustrated manga series. Unlike the other arcs seen in the series, this arc was entirely new and had not been adapted or inspired by what was seen in the anime. This new arc introduced a powerful new villain, new transformations, and more with the tease of an expanded universe from that point on. Which then continued with another arc, Granolah the Survivor.

These arcs were then followed by the manga’s adaptation of the Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero film, and that’s where the manga left off when it went on hiatus back in 2024 . While it had seemed like a suitable ending at the time due to both Toriyama’s passing and the fact that it was also now set at the final story in the Dragon Ball Super timeline, the anime has thrown a wrench into things that only exacerbate one of the lingering cliffhangers that manga fans have yet to see fully resolved. And the anime is going to reach this cliffhanger sooner than not.

The Granolah the Survivor Arc ends with the reveal that Frieza had become the new strongest warrior in the universe after training in a Hyperbolic Time Chamber he stumbled on in space, and this had been the explanation as to why Goku and Vegeta had been seen training together with Broly on Beerus’ planet during Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . With the anime likely eventually adapting this arc after the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc, its also going to hit the wall of that cliffhanger too. It’s just going to be even tougher of a cliffhanger, however, as by that point it will be the final anime story that fans will see.
Dragon Ball Super Just Needs One Last Arc for Fans to Say Goodbye

The only way to avoid this eventual fate is for Dragon Ball Super ‘s manga to return for at least one final arc to resolve the Black Frieza cliffhanger. It would also serve as a perfect way to say goodbye as one last final fight with arguably Dragon Ball ‘s most iconic villain would also be a great way to bookend how far Dragon Ball Super had evolved from its original incarnation. A godly battle against Frieza (and potentially even more ) with Ultra Instinct Goku and Ultra Ego Vegeta at full mastery will also be a big enough fight to feel like it’s fitting of the franchise’s current scale.

Dragon Ball Super basically opened a can of worms when it introduced gods and a multiverse when it first began, and unfortunately will never really be able to tap into the full potential of such an idea even after everything that has happened. Given that the franchise has been under such a tight lock and key since Toriyama’s passing, all fans could probably hope for is at least one final story to help end the series for good. If the manga never does return to settle the Black Frieza story, there’s a potential the anime moves forward with it instead in the coming years. That’s entirely possible given that now the anime team can technically make brand new materials for the series with releases like Dragon Ball Daima seen before , but that was also the final project supervised by Toriyama. It’s been a complicated web of licenses and rights over the last couple of years, but fans just want a sign that the story will get a proper end.

title: Solo Leveling Drops New Look At Jinwoo’s Most Powerful Shadows Ahead of New Movie
content:
While Solo Leveling has yet to share more updates on its anticipated movie, the official X handle drops a new look at Jinwoo’s shadows. The second season wrapped up in March last year, and since then, fans have been anticipating the release window and even a trailer for the movie. While the light novel and webtoon have long since reached their conclusions, the anime still has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The second season wrapped up the Jeju Island Arc , where Jinwoo revealed his true powers in front of the entire world. Things will only continue to get more intense from here on out, and no doubt, Jinwoo will continue to level up even now.

However, along with Jinwoo, his shadows will also continue to become more powerful as they encounter powerful opponents along the way. As of now, Jinwoo has an incredible lineup of powerful shadows that were extracted from the opponents he has defeated so far. His most powerful shadow in the anime so far is Beru, who was previously the Ant King from the S-Rank dungeon on Jeju Island. The official X handle of the anime drops stunning visuals of Jinwoo’s shadows, namely Igris, Beru, Kaisel, Tank, Iron, and Kiba.

Does Solo Leveling Movie Have a Release Date?

Although Solo Leveling: Beyond the System was announced in July during this year’s Anime Expo, the animation studio only shared the concept video and a key visual. While fans are still awaiting a release window, we might get an update next year. The anime will have a theatrical release, which means fans from all over the world will be able to watch the intense fight scenes on the big screen. We can also expect the movie to be released in Japan first before hitting the U.S. theatres a few weeks or months later. Since the movie is being produced by Aniplex, Netmarble, D&C MEDIA, Kakao Piccoma, and Crunchyroll, it’s evident which streaming platform has already acquired rights to the movie.

Solo Leveling: Beyond the System Will Introduce New Challenges for Jinwoo

It’s been confirmed that the movie will pick up from where the second season left off . Jinwoo has already become popular across the world after his feats on Jeju Island were broadcast, which is why Guilds from all over are gunning for him. Following the Jeju Island Arc, the story moves on to the Recruitment Arc, where Jinwoo is getting offers from Guilds to join them, but he has his own plans. Since the Recruitment Arc is one of the shortest in the manhwa, we can also expect the movie to adapt the Ahjin Guild and the Double Dungeon Arcs.

While there hasn’t been any official confirmation on the film’s runtime and how many arcs it will adapt, we can expect it to set the stage for the final phase of the story. The Double Dungeon Arc will especially be more crucial than any other arc in the anime so far, since it carries the answers to several questions about the bizarre world.

Are you excited to see Jinwoo’s power-up in the Solo Leveling movie? Which moment are you anticipating the most? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: New Lilo & Stitch Animated Revival Reveals Sneak Peek Clip Ahead of Release in Theaters
content:
Lilo & Stitch is coming to theaters with an animated revival bringing back the classic franchise for a new generation, and a new sneak peek is showing off the first look at its new short in motion. With Disney’s next major outing, Hexed , hitting theaters over the Thanksgiving holiday teasing it’s going to be the end of one era of Walt Disney Animation Studios , it’s incredibly fitting that screenings of the film are going to be offering a first look at what could end up being the start of the next era for the studio.

Lilo & Scratch is a brand new animated short that will be screening ahead of Hexed , and features the original Lilo & Stitch animated incarnations coming back in a whole new kind of way. The most impressive aspect of the new short is the fact that while it looks like the 2D animated original feature film, it’s actually been animated through the CG animation pipeline at the studio to make a cool new kind of end result. You can check it out in motion below with a special sneak peek clip.

Lilo & Scratch Sneak Peek Clip Released Ahead of Hexed Screenings

Lilo & Scratch will be debuting across theaters on November 25th together with screenings of Disney’s Hexed , so you’re going to want to make it to the theater a bit early to make sure to catch the new short in action. Directed by Malcon Pierce and Fawn Veerasunthorn, it’s the first new animated short from Walt Disney Animation Studios in five years. Using the already set CG animation pipeline with the studio, the new short adapts it to the original 2D animation designs that helps to make it a whole new kind of fluid for a new generation of fans.

Maia Kealoha returns from the live-action Lilo & Stitch and its now in the works sequel as Lilo while Chris Sanders reprises his role as Stitch. As the sneak peek teases, Lilo adopts a mysterious cat that is clearly hiding a rambunctiousness that Stitch is likely going to be contending with in secret. It’s not clear how long this new short will last, but it’s certainly an exciting release given that it lays out a potential future for more of this 2D-like animated releases coming from Disney in the future. Which would be a big deal to the older fans.

When Does Lilo & Stitch 2 Come Out?

Lilo & Stitch’ s live-action feature film reboot had been an incredible success for Disney at the box office, and quickly went into development on its sequel. Lilo & Stitch 2 is currently in the works for a release in Summer 2028 , but a concrete release date has yet to be revealed as of this time. Very little has been revealed for the new sequel, but it’s been confirmed that it will be introducing a new take on Angel, who was one of the many Experiments that had been unleashed in the TV animated series.

Lilo & Stitch ‘s live-action reboot had sparked some debates among fans for some of the changes it had made with its ending, and that’s likely going to continue with the sequel as the stars behind it have teased that it’s also going to make changes from the original version . But with a direct to video sequel and a full TV series to draw inspiration from, it’s likely going to be packed with surprises. How are you liking the look of Lilo & Scratch so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Inklore to Release Tomoko Yamashita's Ikoku Nikki Manga on June 8
content:
Inklore revealed on Wednesday the cover art and June 8, 2027 release for the first volume of Tomoko Yamashita 's Ikoku Nikki manga. The company will release the manga under the English title Ikoku Nikki : Diary of a Strange Land .

Inklore describes the manga's first volume:

Reclusive novelist Makio Koudai has built a life entirely on her own terms—she's sharp-tongued, set in her ways, and far more at ease with the people she invents than the family she keeps at a distance. But everything changes when her older sister dies unexpectedly, leaving behind a now-orphaned daughter, fifteen-year-old Asa. Every door in the family quietly closes but one . . . Makio's. There starts the unsure journey of a prickly aunt and a grieving niece, figuring each other out one awkward day at a time. Can two people who never expected to need each other make room for a life neither of them planned?

Yamashita ( The Night Beyond the Tricornered Window , Don't Cry Girl , Mo'some Sting ) launched the manga in June 2017 in Shodensha 's Feel Young magazine, and ended it in June 2023. The manga's 11th and final compiled book volume shipped in August 2023. The manga was nominated for the 28th Annual Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize in 2024. The manga also ranked at #5 on the women's list of the 2024 edition of Kono Manga ga Sugoi!, topped Da Vinci's 23rd annual "Book of the Year" list for manga in December 2023, and was nominated for the 13th Manga Taisho awards in 2020.

The manga inspired a live-action film that opened in June 2024. The manga then inspired a television anime that debuted on January 4 earlier this year. Crunchyroll streamed the anime with the title Journal with Witch . The anime won one of the four Galaxy Awards for March, and was eventually one of the Encouragement Award winners of the 63rd Galaxy Awards held in June.

Yamashita launched the Tatsumaki manga on Shodensha 's Our Feel web manga site on January 4 earlier this year.

title: Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Season 7 Confirms Disney Release Date – Watch Trailer
content:
Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir is coming back to Disney with a new season, and it’s teasing a big and potentially darker direction for the animated series with the first trailer ahead of its launch later this weekend. Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir has been a massively popular fantasy superhero action series ever since it made its debut, and that has continued even further with tons of new episodes, feature films, spinoffs in development and much more over the years . And it’s coming back for more this month.

Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Season 7 will be coming to the Disney Channel this weekend on Friday, November 20th in the United States to help kick off the global rollout of the new episodes, and it’s teasing new power ups, new transformations, new heroes, new threats, and even a surprsingly dark conspiracy that will challenge Marinette and Adrien more than ever before. You can check out the new trailer for the coming season below for the best look yet and what’s coming our way.

Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Reveals First Look at Season 7

Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Season 7 will be making its debut in the United States and Latin America (following its release in international territories earlier in the month) on the Disney Channel on Friday, November 20th, and then will be available for streaming with Disney+ on November 21st. Produced in collaboration with Disney Kids & Family, Brazil’s Globosat, Italy’s KidsMe and France’s TF1, this new season of the animated series has confirmed it will be running for 26 episodes. And it’s got some big plans for the future of the franchise.

As Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir continues to expand the franchise with all sorts of new projects , it’s been teased that Season 7 will continue to build on the interconnected universe plan for it all moving forward. The wider universe of the series will be expanding in ways fans might not see coming with all sorts of new surprises being set up for the coming season, and naturally Marinette is going to be at the center of it all as she has to deal with a new kind of enemy that’s going to make it tough to keep her life as a hero separate from her personal life.

What to Know for Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Season 7

Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Season 7 teases how Marinette will need to navigate her relationship going forward, “Marinette dreams of enjoying a normal relationship with Adrien, but the secret she carries about his father, Gabriel Agreste, stands in the way. Faced with an impossible choice, she makes a decision that will change everything, affecting her friendships, her relationship with Adrien and her responsibilities as Ladybug.” All the while knowing that a new villain is moving in the shadows with their plan.

Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir is also going to expand its world in a whole new kind of way with a new live-action series now in the works . Miraculous Corp. is working together with See-Saw Films on the new series, but no potential release window or date has been announced as of this time. Are you excited for the new season of Miraculous ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.
